facts.fact: The activity-state wait timeout is 45000 milliseconds.
The steady-state map excludes transient CREATED, STARTED and RESTARTED stages.
close() invokes moveToState(DESTROYED) before removing its lifecycle observer.
The wait compares requested Lifecycle states with the mapped current test Stage and throws after the timeout if no requested steady state is observed.
getCurrentActivityState() maps the current test Stage through STEADY_STATES.
STARTED is a supported request; its implementation first ensures RESUMED, calls pauseActivity(), then waits for the requested state.
moveToState() rejects a null mapped state, explaining the cleanup null-state exception when the last Stage remains transient STARTED.

facts.fact: EmptyFloatingActivity finishes on FINISH_EMPTY_ACTIVITIES and broadcasts EMPTY_FLOATING_ACTIVITY_RESUMED from onResume().
pauseActivity() accepts RESUMED or PAUSED, starts EmptyFloatingActivity with FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK and waits for its resumed broadcast. The helper is intended to leave the target paused.

failure_interpretation.api_usage: moveToState(Lifecycle.State.STARTED) is supported. The existing call is not an API misuse.
failure_interpretation.observed_context: SC10 API34 first attempt reported requested Lifecycle STARTED with last raw test Stage STARTED.
failure_interpretation.source_explanation: Lifecycle STARTED requires steady test Stage PAUSED. A last raw Stage STARTED maps to null and does not satisfy the wait. close() subsequently encounters that same null mapping.
failure_interpretation.exact_floating_helper_divergence_cause: Unestablished. Source semantics explain the assertion and secondary cleanup exception, but do not establish why the device took the observed lifecycle path.

repair_context.intended_flow: Exercise real Home/launcher backgrounding and return to the same activity, with lifecycle and content assertions.
repair_context.distinction: The repair uses Home/launcher backgrounding; it does not replace the request with the CREATED helper.
